docs.title: TERRA Coastal DT
docs.text:
TERRA Coastal DT is the coastal digital twin of the TERRA platform (use case 3). It watches the coastal vegetation edge (VE), the seaward limit of dune vegetation, on Scottish dune coasts. It turns every usable Sentinel-2 scene into a measurement on a fixed set of transects, keeps a monthly history for each site, and forecasts where the edge will be 1 to 24 months ahead, with an uncertainty range.

The forecasts come from a hybrid AI forecaster. A statistical model gives a baseline, and MambaLSTM, a deep sequence model trained on all sites together, learns to correct that baseline's errors.

At a glance

Sites 15 live areas of interest (AOIs) on the east and west coasts of Scotland, in 8 independent coastal groups Observations Sentinel-2 L2A from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, monthly history since 2016, screened for cloud over the AOI itself State variable Vegetation-edge distance along fixed cross-shore transects spaced 15 m apart (metres, seaward positive) Core AI model MambaLSTM: 3 Mamba-style blocks and an LSTM, 192,641 parameters, one model for all sites Forecast p10 / p50 / p90 vegetation-edge lines at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months, plus erosion-risk areas Accuracy 9.2 m RMSE at 1 month and 10.9 m at 12 months on held-out data; best of all methods tested at every horizon State storage MongoDB and MinIO: observations, forecasts, datasets and model versions with full provenance

docs.title: How the digital twin works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Sentinel-2 L2A<br/>(CDSE)"] --> B["Acquisition and<br/>AOI cloud screening"]
    B --> C["Vegetation-edge<br/>extraction on<br/>fixed transects"]
    C --> D["Monthly VE history<br/>per transect"]
    D --> E["Statistical base<br/>refitted per request"]
    D --> F["MambaLSTM<br/>learned correction"]
    E --> G["Hybrid forecast<br/>p10 / p50 / p90"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Maps, erosion risk,<br/>validation, API"]
    H -. "new observation" .-> B
  1. Observe. New Sentinel-2 scenes are found, screened for cloud over the AOI, and downloaded (Satellite Image Processing, Data Ingestion).
  2. Measure. The vegetation edge is extracted on the AOI's fixed reference line and transects, so every date is measured in the same frame (Vegetation Edge Extraction).
  3. Remember. Accepted observations become monthly per-transect series, stored with their provenance (Data & State Model).
  4. Forecast. The statistical base is refitted on the whole record at every request, and MambaLSTM adds its learned correction (MambaLSTM Forecasting Model).
  5. Check. Retrospective validation reruns the forecast from earlier dates and compares it with what was later observed (Retrospective Validation).

docs.title: Why MambaLSTM
docs.text:
The baseline captures the slow trend, the seasonal cycle and short-term memory of each transect. What it cannot capture is the information in a transect's neighbourhood and recent history: for example, a stretch of coast that has sat seaward of its long-term level for a year tends to stay there, and a fast-moving stretch tends to slow down. MambaLSTM reads a 12-month window of the baseline's errors across a 390 m stretch of coast (27 neighbouring transects) and learns these patterns across all 15 sites at once.

On data the model never saw during training, the hybrid reduces RMSE against the baseline by 2.9 to 6.5%, against a plain LSTM by 3.3 to 10.7%, and against "no change" by 9.3 to 33.2%. A per-horizon gate ensures the correction is only applied as far as it has proven useful. See Training & Evaluation.

docs.title: API Surface
docs.text: TERRA Coastal DT exposes a JSON HTTP API used by its web interface, by the TERRA platform workflows and by integrators. The service publishes its own OpenAPI description at /openapi.yaml; a copy is available here as openapi.yaml.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Requests and responses are JSON. Most responses carry success and, on failure, an error message.
  • Long-running work returns 202 Accepted with a job identifier; poll GET /jobs/<job_id> for phase events and the result.
  • Job submissions accept an idempotency_key, so a retried request returns the existing job.
  • Map outputs are GeoJSON in WGS 84; distances are metres along transects, positive seaward.
  • Downloads redirect to short-lived presigned object-storage links.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• /models/* (promotion and rollback) requires an administrator bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • User and service authentication is handled by the TERRA platform gateway in front of the service.

docs.title: Typical forecast sequence
docs.text:
1. GET /aoi/prepared: list AOIs available for forecasting.
  2. GET /aoi/<aoi_id>/geometry/fixed: load the reference line and transects.
  3. POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/extract/latest: extract the newest usable observation.
  4. POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/history/context: load the historical context.
  5. POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/forecast/latest: forecast from that observation.
  6. Display the returned layers; fetch artifacts through GET /artifacts/<artifact_id>.

docs.title: Observation and forecast
docs.text:
Route Body (main fields) Purpose POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/extract/latest force_refresh Search, screen and extract the newest usable scene; reuses a cached observation when nothing newer exists POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/history/context years, month Historical context for the forecast page POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/history/coastlines years (default 5), month Same-month vegetation-edge lines for the last N years and their net change POST /aoi/<aoi_id>/forecast/latest run_id, profile (yearly or semiannual), steps_ahead Forecast from the latest observation. The horizon is 12 or 6 months times steps_ahead

A forecast response for a MambaLSTM AOI includes the p10 / p50 / p90 GeoJSON lines, the uncertainty band, erosion-risk polygons and a forecast_method block with the base and correction components, the gate, the network horizon, interval calibration, the horizon_extrapolated flag and model_skill (the deployed model's test RMSE at this AOI).

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
A workflow that cannot complete returns a diagnostic rather than a partial result. Common causes:

  • no recent scene passed AOI-level cloud screening or extraction;
  • the imagery provider is unavailable;
  • the AOI has no fixed geometry or not enough history;
  • storage is unavailable (503 from readiness and storage-backed routes);
  • an administrator token is missing or wrong (403 on /models/*).

docs.title: Service Architecture
docs.text:
TERRA Coastal DT runs as one stateless service container next to shared MongoDB and MinIO stores. Durable state (observations, forecasts, datasets, model versions and artifacts) lives in the stores, so the container can be replaced or restarted at any time.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Responsibility Documentation Satellite image processing Catalogue search, AOI-level cloud screening, download, preflight checks Satellite Image Processing Vegetation-edge extraction Fixed geometry, classification, per-transect edge selection, temporal prior, quality control Vegetation Edge Extraction Time-series analysis and forecasting Monthly series, MambaLSTM hybrid forecasts, erosion risk, historical coastlines Time-Series Forecasting, MambaLSTM Digital twin orchestration Assimilation, jobs, state, model registry, web interface and API DT Orchestration Data ingestion profile The UC3 acquisition profile run by the TERRA ingestion service Data Ingestion

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
• One process, many threads. The service runs under gunicorn with one worker and several threads. Jobs run on an in-process executor, so a single process keeps job ownership simple.
  • Stateless container. Downloaded datasets, model packages and the vegetation classifier are cached locally only after their checksums are verified, and can be deleted at any time.
  • Database-first reads. AOIs, geometry, observations, datasets and active model versions are read from MongoDB; large objects are fetched from MinIO.
  • Provenance everywhere. Observations carry a pipeline signature, and forecasts record the model version, dataset version and observation they were made from.

docs.title: Shared storage and namespacing
docs.text: Every record is scoped by project and use case. In a shared platform database, UC3's collections carry the uc3_ prefix, and its objects live under their own prefix in the shared bucket, so UC3 cannot read or overwrite other use cases' data. The service refuses to start against a shared database without the approved prefix, and never creates or alters collections there automatically.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Credentials (CDSE, MongoDB, MinIO, admin token) come only from environment variables or mounted secret files; none are stored in code or images.
  • Model administration (/models/*) requires an administrator bearer token. Other routes are intended to sit behind the platform gateway, which handles user authentication.
  • Downloads are short-lived presigned MinIO links, so the service never streams large files itself.
  • The container runs as a non-root user.

docs.title: Technology
docs.text: Layer Technology Service Python 3.10, Flask, gunicorn Geospatial rasterio, pyproj, shapely, scikit-image AI model PyTorch (CPU inference), MambaLSTM Storage MongoDB (replica set), MinIO (S3-compatible) Orchestration Apache Airflow (TERRA platform) Packaging Docker image published to the GitHub Container Registry

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All configuration comes from environment variables, so the same image runs locally, in staging and in production.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Credentials are never stored in code, images or this documentation. Every secret can be passed either directly or as a file through a <NAME>_FILE variable (for example MINIO_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/minio_secret_key), which suits Docker and orchestrator secrets.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Variable Purpose TERRA_STORAGE_BACKEND mongo_minio for deployments; local (files only) for development TERRA_PROJECT_ID, TERRA_USE_CASE_ID Scope of every stored record (UC3) MONGODB_URI, MONGODB_DATABASE MongoDB connection (secret) and database TERRA_MONGODB_COLLECTION_PREFIX Collection prefix; uc3_ is required in a shared database MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY Object storage connection (keys are secrets) MINIO_BUCKET, MINIO_PREFIX Bucket and the UC3 object prefix within it MINIO_REGION Set it to avoid a bucket-location lookup that prefix-scoped keys may not be allowed MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT Address browsers use for presigned downloads, if different from the internal one MINIO_SECURE, MINIO_CERT_CHECK TLS settings TERRA_PRESIGNED_EXPIRY_SECONDS Lifetime of download links (900 s by default) TERRA_AUTO_INITIALIZE_STORAGE Create collections at start-up; refused in a shared database

The service refuses to start against a shared database or bucket without the approved prefix.

docs.title: Imagery and extraction
docs.text: Variable Purpose CDSE_CLIENT_ID, CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET Copernicus Data Space credentials for on-demand latest-scene search (secrets); leave empty to disable TERRA_LATEST_MAX_AOI_CLOUD_PCT AOI-level cloud limit for the latest scene TERRA_LATEST_OBSERVATION_CACHE_SECONDS How long a repeated latest-observation request reuses the stored result without a catalogue call TERRA_VE_EXTRACTION_ALGORITHM Extraction algorithm (peak_preserving_v3 by default) TERRA_VE_CLASSIFIER_SHA256 Expected checksum of the vegetation classifier loaded from storage

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
Variable Purpose TERRA_CODE_REVISION, TERRA_CONTAINER_DIGEST Identity of the extraction pipeline, part of every observation's signature

These describe the pipeline that produced the stored history, not merely the running image. Keeping them equal to the history's values means new observations get the same signature as the history; changing them would treat the new pipeline as different and duplicate observations.

docs.title: Model, jobs and administration
docs.text: Variable Purpose TERRA_MODEL_ADMIN_TOKEN Bearer token for /models/* promotion and rollback (secret) TERRA_JOB_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS When an unfinished job from a stopped process is marked failed TERRA_DT_ENABLE_SCHEDULER In-process scheduler; off in staging and production, where Airflow schedules work TERRA_MATERIALIZED_CACHE_DIR Local cache for verified datasets and model packages (disposable)

docs.title: Service
docs.text: Variable Purpose TERRA_HOST, TERRA_PORT Bind address and port (5000 by default)

docs.title: Effect on users
docs.text:
• Without imagery credentials, the latest-observation step reports the provider as unavailable; forecasts from stored observations still work.
  • Without storage, readiness reports 503 and storage-backed routes return diagnostics.
  • An AOI without an active model is not listed for forecasting.

docs.title: Data Ingestion
docs.text:
In the TERRA platform, satellite data is acquired by a shared ingestion service that runs one profile per use case. TERRA Coastal DT provides its profile, coastal-uc3-sentinel2, as a standalone Python package (terra-wp2-uc3-ingestion). The package needs no part of the digital twin itself (no Flask, no PyTorch, no models), so the ingestion service can install it on its own.

sequenceDiagram
    participant AF as Airflow
    participant ING as Ingestion service<br/>(profile coastal-uc3-sentinel2)
    participant CDSE as Copernicus Data Space
    participant ST as MongoDB + MinIO
    participant DT as Coastal DT service
    AF->>ING: run (AOI, time window, selection policy)
    ING->>CDSE: catalogue search
    ING->>CDSE: AOI-level SCL probe per candidate
    ING->>CDSE: 5-band download of accepted scenes
    ING->>ING: structural and coastal preflight checks
    ING->>ST: commit scenes, scene assets, artifacts
    ING-->>AF: result: completed / no_data / failed
    AF->>DT: POST /jobs/assimilate (scene_asset_ids)
    AF->>DT: GET /jobs/<job_id> until done

docs.title: Division of responsibilities
docs.text:
Ingestion profile Coastal DT service Catalogue search, AOI cloud screening, download Fixed geometry and vegetation-edge extraction Structural and coastal preflight checks Scientific quality control and observation acceptance Commits scene assets (rasters and their metadata) Observations, datasets, models, forecasts, risk products Holds the CDSE and storage credentials of the ingestion deployment Owns the AOI registry and supplies AOI values per request

The profile never writes observations, models, forecasts or geometry. It only delivers scene assets, which the digital twin then assimilates.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
All documents are validated against JSON schemas (JSON Schema 2020-12) shipped inside the package.

Document Purpose Acquisition request (v2) AOI, time window (latest or explicit), selection policy, retry identity Scene package (v2) One delivered asset: scene identity, acquisition time, AOI screening statistics, raster description, asset fingerprint and provenance Ingestion result (v2) Outcome and the committed scene asset identifiers Assimilation request The body sent to POST /jobs/assimilate

Key rules:

  • Three explicit outcomes. completed (new assets committed), no_data (nothing suitable: a normal outcome, skipped quietly), failed (a provider or storage error worth retrying).
  • Exact scene binding. Each download is bound to the catalogue acquisition time within ±3 minutes, so an asset always means one satellite pass.
  • Retry identity. A request's identity is derived from its content (project, AOI, window, policy), never from attempt time, so retries do not create duplicate assets.
  • Reuse before download. An asset already committed for the same scene and AOI is reused.
  • Versioned meaning. A change to what an asset means requires a new contract version; older requests are refused with an explanation rather than silently reinterpreted.

docs.title: Selection policies
docs.text: Policy AOI cloud limit Use uc3_parity_pilot 10% unusable pixels; tile pre-filter 80%; up to 24 candidates probed; at most 3 scenes Latest-observation updates uc3_monthly_backfill 20% unusable pixels Filling historical months

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: The profile writes only three collections (scenes, scene_assets, artifacts, with the uc3_ prefix in a shared database) and objects under the scene-input prefix of UC3's storage area. A deployment guard refuses to publish into the digital twin's live namespace unless that is explicitly allowed.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: All settings come from UC3_INGEST_* environment variables (CDSE client, MongoDB, MinIO, project, namespace). There are no built-in defaults for storage targets, so a misconfigured deployment fails instead of writing to the wrong place.

docs.title: Data & State Model
docs.text: TERRA Coastal DT keeps the state of each coastal site as versioned records in MongoDB and immutable objects in MinIO. Every observation is expressed in the AOI's fixed measurement frame, so current, historical and forecast states are directly comparable.

docs.title: Measurement frame
docs.text:
• AOI: a registered coastal box with a name, coastal group, coordinate reference system and lifecycle status (active or retired).
  • Geometry version: one reference line and its transects (15 m spacing). Changes create a new version rather than editing the old one.
  • Distance: a vegetation-edge position is the signed distance in metres along a transect from the reference line, positive seaward.

docs.title: State records (MongoDB)
docs.text:
Collection Holds aois AOI geometry, bounding box, CRS and lifecycle status geometry_versions Versioned reference line and transect packages transects Per-transect documents scenes Satellite scene metadata and catalogue status scene_assets AOI-specific scene assets (the 5-band rasters) committed by acquisition scene_evaluations Accepted and rejected candidate scenes, with reasons observations Historical and live vegetation-edge observations, with pipeline signature and review status transect_measurements Per-transect VE distances of each observation (queryable) digital_twin_states Latest-state snapshots per AOI forecasts Forecast requests, signatures, provenance and output references forecast_measurements Per-transect p10 / p50 / p90 distances and erosion-risk flags dataset_versions Monthly dataset snapshots used for forecasting and training model_versions Model packages, lifecycle status (candidate, active, superseded) and evaluation training_runs Candidate training runs and their evaluation runs, run_events Job state and ordered phase events artifacts Registry of every MinIO object: checksum, state and lineage migration_ledger Record of storage migrations

Common fields (project_id, use_case_id, schema_version, created_at, updated_at) scope and version every record. Collections have JSON-schema validators and unique indexes, created by an idempotent initialisation step.

docs.title: Objects (MinIO)
docs.text:
Object family Examples Scene inputs 5-band AOI rasters and previews Run outputs VE lines and points, intersections, time-series tables, forecast GeoJSON Datasets Monthly patch series per AOI Models MambaLSTM packages (weights, gates, calibration, validation report) Classifier The vegetation classifier, verified by checksum

Objects are immutable: a changed product is a new object, registered in artifacts with its checksum. Users receive short-lived presigned links for downloads.

docs.title: Versioning and provenance
docs.text:
What How it is versioned Geometry New geometry version for any change; observations reference the version they were measured on Observations Pipeline signature: code revision, container image, extraction algorithm and classifier checksum. An identical request reuses the existing observation Datasets New dataset version per rebuild; extraction parameters are pinned on the version Models New model version per package; promotion and rollback switch the active version together with its dataset Forecasts Signature of observation, dataset and model; an identical forecast request reuses the stored result

This makes every forecast reproducible: it can be traced to the exact observation, dataset, model and code that produced it.

docs.title: Public data boundary
docs.text: This documentation describes data structures and products. Credentials, private infrastructure details and unpublished datasets are not part of the public site.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: TERRA Coastal DT is delivered as a Docker image and runs as one container next to MongoDB and MinIO. This page describes what a deployment needs and how the pieces fit; environment-specific values belong in the deployment's private configuration, not here.

docs.title: Service image
docs.text:
Registry GitHub Container Registry, published from version tags of the source repository Base Python 3.10 (slim), CPU build of PyTorch Process gunicorn, 1 worker with 8 threads, 600 s request timeout Port 5000 User Non-root Contents Code, web interface and AOI registry only; no data, models or credentials

Release images should be built from a commit (for example from git archive), so file permissions inside the image are normalised and the image matches a recorded code revision.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• MongoDB (replica set) with an account that has read-write access to the UC3 collections.
  • MinIO (or S3-compatible storage) with a bucket, or a prefix of a shared bucket, for UC3 objects.
  • Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem credentials, if the service should fetch the latest scenes on demand.
  • Published data: AOIs, geometry versions, observation history, datasets, the active MambaLSTM model package and the vegetation classifier, loaded into the stores before the service starts.
  • A reverse proxy or gateway that authenticates users and routes to the service. The web interface uses absolute paths, so it needs its own host name or port rather than a sub-path, and long extraction requests need a read timeout of about 600 s.

docs.title: Deployment steps
docs.text:
1. Initialise storage. Run the initialisation tool in plan mode (read-only), then apply it. It creates missing collections, validators and indexes, skips what already matches, and stops without writing if an existing collection differs. In a shared database it touches only the uc3_-prefixed collections.
  2. Publish domain data. Load AOIs, geometry, history, datasets and the model package into MongoDB and MinIO. Publishing is idempotent.
  3. Configure the container through environment variables and secret files (see Configuration), including the provenance values of the extraction pipeline the history was built with.
  4. Start the container and check GET /health/ready. It reports 200 only when MongoDB, the UC3 collections and MinIO are reachable.
  5. Smoke test: list prepared AOIs, load fixed geometry, run a forecast and download an artifact.

docs.title: Deployment patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Use Local TERRA node Development and demonstration against a local MongoDB and MinIO in Docker Platform staging Integration with the TERRA Airflow and ingestion services Shared platform storage Production next to the TERRA shared data layer: UC3 collections under the uc3_ prefix and objects under their own bucket prefix, isolated from other use cases

The service's in-process scheduler stays disabled in staging and production; Airflow is the control plane.

docs.title: Moving between stores
docs.text: A migration tool moves an existing UC3 store into a shared one: it inventories source and target, dumps the source database, restores it under the new collection prefix, copies objects, rewrites object references and verifies counts and checksums. Pipeline signatures are preserved, so migrated history stays consistent with new observations.

docs.title: What is TERRA Coastal DT?
docs.text: The coastal digital twin of the TERRA platform. It measures the vegetation edge of dune coasts from Sentinel-2 imagery, keeps a monthly history for each site, forecasts the edge 1 to 24 months ahead with uncertainty, and validates those forecasts against later observations.

docs.title: Which sites are covered?
docs.text: 15 live AOIs on the east and west coasts of Scotland, from St Andrews West Sands to Morrich More, in 8 independent coastal groups.

docs.title: What is a transect?
docs.text: A fixed cross-shore line along which the vegetation edge is measured. Transects are spaced 15 m apart, and distances are in metres from the AOI's reference line, positive seaward.

docs.title: Why the vegetation edge and not the waterline?
docs.text: The waterline moves by tens of metres with tide, waves and surge within hours. The vegetation edge reflects erosion and accretion over months and years, which is the change that matters for coastal management.

docs.title: What is MambaLSTM?
docs.text: The core AI model of the digital twin: a deep sequence model with three Mamba-style blocks (causal convolution with gating) followed by an LSTM, 192,641 parameters in total. It reads 12 months of a statistical forecast's errors across 27 neighbouring transects (390 m of coast), plus 16 context features, and predicts the error of the next forecast. See MambaLSTM Forecasting Model.

docs.title: Why not let the neural network forecast the coast directly?
docs.text: Because a closed-form model already captures level, seasonality and short-term memory well and adapts instantly to new data. Asking the network to learn only what that model misses makes it smaller, safer (predicting zero reproduces the base) and more accurate. Against a plain LSTM that forecasts directly from a transect's history, the hybrid's RMSE is 3 to 11% lower.

docs.title: How much does MambaLSTM improve the forecast?
docs.text: On held-out test data it reduces RMSE against the statistical base by 2.9 to 6.5%, most at 12 and 24 months, and the hybrid is the most accurate of all methods tested at every horizon. See Training & Evaluation.

docs.title: What if the network learns something that does not generalise?
docs.text: A per-horizon gate, fitted on held-out data, scales the correction between 0 and 1. Where the correction does not help, the gate shrinks it and the forecast falls back to the statistical base.

docs.title: Is there one model per site?
docs.text: No. One MambaLSTM serves all 15 AOIs; each site's behaviour enters through its own data. Training on all sites together gives the network far more examples than any single site's record.

docs.title: Does the model need retraining when new images arrive?
docs.text: No. The statistical base is refitted on the whole record at every forecast, so new observations count immediately. The shared network is retrained occasionally, when substantial new history or new sites are added.

docs.title: What does the forecast show?
docs.text: The median forecast edge (p50), an 80% interval (p10 to p90) and, optionally, erosion-risk areas where even the conservative p10 forecast lies landward of today's edge.

docs.title: How reliable is the uncertainty band?
docs.text: On test data the nominal 80% band contains 72 to 76% of outcomes, so it is slightly narrow. Treat it as a guide to relative certainty along the coast rather than an exact probability.

docs.title: What about horizons beyond two years?
docs.text: They are produced but flagged horizon_extrapolated, because the intervals are calibrated only up to 24 months.

docs.title: Are forecasts decisions?
docs.text: No. They are decision support, to be read alongside local knowledge, expert assessment and other evidence. Storms, surges and coastal works are not yet model inputs.

docs.title: Why might the latest observation fail?
docs.text: Recent scenes may be too cloudy over the AOI, the imagery provider may be unavailable, or extraction may not find a reliable edge. The page reports which.

docs.title: What does retrospective validation mean?
docs.text: The forecast is rerun from the same month one or more years earlier, using only data available then, and compared with today's observation. Each case also scores the statistical base, a trend model and a plain LSTM.

docs.title: Why might a validation case be missing?
docs.text: No usable scene in that month, scenes rejected by screening or quality control, history not yet extracted, or a look-back window that is too short. The backfill plan explains the cause.

docs.title: How does data reach the digital twin in the platform?
docs.text: The TERRA ingestion service runs the UC3 acquisition profile, commits screened scenes to shared storage, and Airflow asks the digital twin to assimilate them. See Data Ingestion.

docs.title: Where is the OpenAPI description?
docs.text: The service publishes it at /openapi.yaml; a copy is available here as openapi.yaml.

docs.title: Forecast Workflow
docs.text: The main web page (/) takes a user from a coastal site to a forecast in five steps. Every step works in the AOI's fixed measurement frame, so the current edge, its history and the forecast can be compared directly on the map.

docs.title: Step 1: Select AOI
docs.text: Choose one of the live AOIs. The list shows only AOIs with fixed geometry and an active forecast model; retired AOIs are hidden. The map zooms to the AOI and draws its reference line and transects.

docs.title: Step 2: Latest observation and current VE
docs.text:
Extract Latest Observation searches recent Sentinel-2 scenes, screens them for cloud over the AOI, and extracts the vegetation edge from the newest usable scene. The page shows:

  • the accepted scene preview on the map;
  • the current vegetation edge;
  • the acquisition date, imagery source and run identifier.

If the latest usable scene has already been processed, the stored observation is returned without reprocessing. If no recent scene passes screening, the page explains why.

docs.title: Step 3: Historical context
docs.text: Load Historical Context loads the AOI's monthly vegetation-edge record used by the forecaster, and reports the number of historical observations and the earliest and latest dates.

docs.title: Step 4: Transect forecast
docs.text:
Choose a horizon in years and select Run Transect Forecast. The MambaLSTM hybrid forecaster (see MambaLSTM Forecasting Model):

  1. adds the observation from Step 2 to the AOI's record;
  2. refits the statistical base on the whole record;
  3. applies the gated MambaLSTM correction for every transect;
  4. adds the calibrated p10 and p90 bounds.

The map shows:

Layer Meaning Current VE The edge extracted in Step 2 Forecast p50 The median forecast edge p10 / p90 The bounds of the 80% forecast interval Uncertainty band The area between p10 and p90 Erosion risk (toggle) Areas where even the conservative p10 forecast lies landward of the current edge

The status line reports the deployed model's held-out RMSE for this AOI at the chosen horizon, so each forecast comes with an honest error scale. Horizons beyond two years are produced but flagged as extrapolated, because the intervals are calibrated up to 24 months.

docs.title: Step 5: Historical coastline change
docs.text: Choose how many past years to show (1 to 15). The page draws the vegetation edge in the same calendar month of each year, from lightest (earliest) to deepest red (latest), and reports the median net change between the first and last year, positive seaward. Using the same month every year keeps the seasonal cycle out of the comparison.

docs.title: Why fixed geometry matters
docs.text: The reference line and transects are fixed before anything is measured or forecast. A change in the reported distance therefore means the vegetation edge moved, not that the measurement frame changed.

docs.title: Keeping the digital twin current
docs.text: New observations need no manual step in a platform deployment: the daily workflow acquires new scenes and assimilates them, and the next forecast refits the statistical base on the updated record. The MambaLSTM weights do not need to change for new months to count.

docs.title: Adding an AOI
docs.text:
config/aois.json in the source repository is the single source of truth for AOI extents, names, coastal groups and status. To add a site:

  1. Register the AOI with its bounding box and coastal group.
  2. Pull history: monthly Sentinel-2 scenes from 2016 with AOI-level cloud screening.
  3. Build geometry: a reference line from the temporal composite, an orientation check, and transects every 15 m. Check the largest gap between the vegetation edge and the reference line first, and set transect reach with about 100 m of margin.
  4. Extract the vegetation edge for every scene, with the temporal prior.
  5. Run the signal gate. If the record carries no forecastable signal, stop: the AOI should not be forecast.
  6. Build the monthly dataset.
  7. Retrain the MambaLSTM correction on all AOIs, and compare the test report with the active model's (see Model Lifecycle).
  8. Publish the AOI, geometry, history, dataset and model to the stores.

docs.title: Correcting geometry
docs.text: When a reference line is wrong for a stretch of coast (it runs past the end of a beach, or cuts across a hook so transects run along the edge), the correction is made as a new geometry version: the line is trimmed or rerouted, the affected history is re-extracted, the dataset rebuilt and the model retrained. Past geometry versions are kept, so earlier observations stay traceable.

docs.title: Retiring an AOI
docs.text: Set its status to retired. It disappears from the web interface and the platform's AOI list, while its records stay in storage.

docs.title: Retraining the model
docs.text: Retrain the shared MambaLSTM correction when several months of new history have accumulated across AOIs, when AOIs are added, or after geometry corrections. Always compare the new rolling-origin report with the active one before promoting, and keep the previous package for rollback.

docs.title: Operational monitoring
docs.text:
Signal Where Service and dependency health GET /health/live, GET /health/ready Job failures and stale jobs GET /jobs/<job_id>, job phase events Scene rejections and their reasons Scene evaluations, observation history Gaps in an AOI's record Time-series status, validation backfill plan Model state GET /aois/<aoi_id>/model-status

Diagnostics separate system errors from missing imagery and from low-quality observations; only the first needs operator action.

docs.title: Documentation updates
docs.text: Update this site whenever user workflows, the public API, the model or deployment assumptions change, and publish it as a new version with the Deploy Docs workflow.

docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text: Quality assurance covers four layers: the code, the observations, the model and the deployment.

docs.title: Automated tests
docs.text:
Suite Scope Service tests API contracts, web pages, extraction quality control, hybrid forecaster, validation service, storage settings and isolation, provenance and downloads Ingestion package tests Contract schemas and examples, catalogue handling, AOI screening, raster preflight, orchestration decisions; fully offline with synthetic rasters Storage contract tests Run against throwaway authenticated MongoDB and MinIO instances, never against live stores

Tests that need live services are skipped when those are not configured, so the suites run anywhere.

docs.title: Observation quality
docs.text:
• AOI-level cloud screening before download, and structural and coastal preflight checks after.
  • Extraction quality control: per-scene transect coverage, reach limits from the reference line, and the temporal prior against single-scene failures.
  • Signal gate for every AOI before it is forecast.
  • Review: operators can record a review decision for any observation.
  • Rejection records: every rejected scene keeps its reasons.

docs.title: Model quality
docs.text:
• Rolling-origin evaluation with no look-ahead: the most recent 24 months of every AOI are held out, and metrics are averaged per origin, then per AOI.
  • Comparison with baselines in every evaluation: persistence, trend only, a plain LSTM and the statistical base.
  • Per-horizon gates limit the MambaLSTM correction to where it has proven useful.
  • Interval coverage is reported for every horizon (72 to 76% for a nominal 80%).
  • Independent window: the protocol can be repeated on an earlier period to check that rankings hold.
  • Shared code for training and serving: model inputs are built by the same functions, so the deployed model sees exactly what it was evaluated on.

See Training & Evaluation for the results.

docs.title: Provenance and reproducibility
docs.text:
• Every observation carries a pipeline signature; every forecast records its observation, dataset and model versions.
  • Identical requests reuse stored results rather than recomputing them.
  • Objects are immutable and checksummed; cached copies are verified before use.

docs.title: Workflow checks
docs.text: Before a release, the main workflows are checked end to end on a live AOI: select an AOI, load geometry, extract or reuse the latest observation, load history, forecast with bounds and erosion risk, compare historical coastlines, run validation cases, and download an artifact.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: Automated checks support interpretation but do not replace expert judgement. Storms, engineering works, sediment supply and vegetation management can change a coast in ways an automated forecast does not capture.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: This page explains the main technical decisions behind TERRA Coastal DT and the evidence that shaped them.

docs.title: 1. Coastal state as a digital twin variable
docs.text:
The digital twin treats the coastline as an evolving state, not as a line extracted from one image. For each AOI it maintains:

  • a fixed measurement frame (reference line and transects);
  • the observed vegetation-edge history on that frame;
  • the latest observed state;
  • forecasts with uncertainty, and evidence of how well past forecasts did.

docs.title: 2. The vegetation edge as the state variable
docs.text: The waterline moves by tens of metres with tide, waves and surge within hours. The vegetation edge moves with erosion and accretion over months and years, which is the change coastal management needs to track. It is the primary state variable; other lines are supporting information only.

docs.title: 3. A fixed measurement frame
docs.text:
Observations from different dates must be measured in the same frame, or real change gets mixed with changes in the frame.

  • The reference line is traced on a temporal median composite of many clear scenes. This replaced an earlier approach that seeded the line from one scene with a segmentation network: the network failed on coasts it had not seen, its traced boundary followed the image border where vegetation reached it, and a single date biased the datum at sites with a trend. The composite needs no trained model and sits at the long-term mean edge.
  • Transects every 15 m give a dense, regular alongshore grid, oriented positive seaward.
  • Site-specific problems (a line ending beyond the beach, a hook the line cut across, a spit tip) are fixed as new geometry versions, not by changing the history.

docs.title: 4. Robust extraction
docs.text:
Scenes acquired within the same month, when the coast has not really moved, show the structure of extraction error. Extraction is precise most of the time (median repeat difference 3.2 m, a third of a Sentinel-2 pixel), but when it fails, it fails coherently over runs of neighbouring transects. A coherent run looks smooth alongshore, so spatial smoothing alone cannot catch it; time can, because a run that is wrong in one scene is right in its neighbours in time. The extraction design reflects that:

  • candidates from several cues (threshold crossing, contour, gradient) on each transect;
  • joint alongshore selection with a smoothness penalty, preserving well-supported headlands and spits;
  • a leave-one-out temporal prior over the nearest scenes in time, which roughly halved the noise floor at every AOI while preserving known trends;
  • a signal gate before any AOI is forecast: if month-to-month differences show that the record is mostly measurement noise, no model can forecast it, and the AOI is not used.

docs.title: 5. Transect distances, not image masks
docs.text: Forecasting distances along fixed transects, rather than future image masks, gives values with physical meaning (metres), uses the same frame for history, present and future, makes missing or weak transects visible, and turns uncertainty into lower, median and upper lines on the map.

docs.title: 6. Monthly composites at native spacing
docs.text:
Each month's accepted scenes are combined into a per-transect median, and values that disagree strongly with their alongshore neighbours are removed. The series keep the native 15 m transect spacing, and gaps stay missing values that the model masks.

An earlier design resampled every coastline to a fixed grid and compressed it with principal components. It was dropped: the fixed grid made the same position mean a different place at each AOI and forced gaps to be filled in. The measured alongshore correlation length, 90 to 105 m at every AOI, sets instead the patch width, the outlier-rejection window and the smoothing scale. Because the patch layout does not depend on coastline length, AOIs of any size share one model.

docs.title: 7. A hybrid AI forecaster
docs.text:
The forecaster combines a statistical base with the MambaLSTM deep sequence model:

  • The base captures level, seasonal cycle and short-term memory, refitted on the whole record at every request, so new observations count immediately.
  • The trend sets the level but is not extrapolated. Trends fitted on the two halves of a record correlate at only -0.49 to +0.33. Dropping trend extrapolation cut 24-month error by 9 to 16% in two independent test windows.
  • MambaLSTM learns the base's errors from a year of residuals across 27 neighbouring transects and 16 context features, shared across all AOIs. It finds what the base cannot: persistent level offsets (40 to 60% of a year-long offset persists into 12 to 24-month targets) and trend reversion (about half the fitted trend).
  • A per-horizon gate scales the correction by its proven usefulness on held-out data, so the hybrid falls back to the base wherever the network adds nothing.
  • Calibrated intervals come from conformal error quantiles per AOI and horizon.

docs.title: 8. Evaluation without look-ahead
docs.text: Every result is produced under a rolling-origin protocol: each forecast uses only data up to its own origin, the most recent 24 months of every AOI are held out for testing, and metrics are averaged per origin and then per AOI. This protocol exposed that an earlier static baseline's apparent skill came from look-ahead, and it is the basis for every reported number. Under it, the hybrid is the most accurate of all methods tested at every horizon (see Training & Evaluation).

docs.title: 9. Database-first digital twin
docs.text: State lives in MongoDB and MinIO, not in the service container. Observations, datasets, models and forecasts are versioned and linked by signatures, so every forecast can be traced to the observation, dataset, model and code that produced it, and an identical request reuses the stored result.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Accuracy depends on clear-sky imagery; long cloudy periods leave gaps.
  • The model uses only the coastline's own history; storms, surges and wave climate are not yet inputs.
  • Uncertainty intervals are slightly narrow (72 to 76% coverage for a nominal 80%).
  • The approach is validated on Scottish dune coasts; other settings need their own validation.
  • Forecasts are decision support and should be read alongside local knowledge and expert assessment.

docs.title: Retrospective Validation
docs.text: The validation page (/validation) answers a practical question: if the digital twin had issued a forecast one or two years ago, how close would it have been to what is observed today? It also shows how the MambaLSTM hybrid compares with simpler methods on the same case.

docs.title: How a case works
docs.text:
1. Ground truth. The latest extracted observation of the AOI is the target.
  2. Cut-offs. The service finds earlier years with an observation in the same calendar month as the target (within a look-back window, five years by default) and suggests cases, for example one year and two years before the target.
  3. Re-forecast. For each case, the forecaster is run from the cut-off month using only data up to that month, exactly as it would have seen the record then.
  4. Score. Each case's forecast is compared with the target on every transect, and shown as map overlays and error metrics.

Same-month cut-offs keep the seasonal cycle out of the comparison: a one-year case forecasts from the same season it is scored against.

docs.title: Methods scored in every case
docs.text:
For MambaLSTM AOIs, each case scores several methods from the same origin:

Method What it shows Hybrid (MambaLSTM) The deployed forecaster Base The statistical base without the MambaLSTM correction: the value added by the network Trend A straight per-transect trend, extrapolated Naive LSTM A plain LSTM on the transect's own history

Persistence ("no change") is not offered as a method on this page. At same-month horizons on slowly changing coasts it mainly reflects how little the edge moved; its rolling-origin results are reported in Training & Evaluation.

docs.title: One case is one draw
docs.text: A single retrospective case is one sample of forecast error and can favour any method by chance. The page therefore also shows model_skill: the deployed model's rolling-origin test RMSE at this AOI, computed over every forecast origin in the 24-month test period. That is the statistically meaningful number; the cases make it visible on the map.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: When an expected cut-off year is missing, the backfill plan explains why: no imagery in that month, scenes rejected by cloud screening or extraction quality, history not yet extracted, or a window too short. It also suggests how to recover the missing months.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: Validation does not guarantee future accuracy. It shows whether the forecaster has behaved consistently on recent history, how error grows with horizon, and where on the coast forecasts tend to miss.

docs.title: MambaLSTM Forecasting Model
docs.text:
MambaLSTM is the core AI model of TERRA Coastal DT. It is a deep sequence model that reads the recent history of a stretch of coast and predicts how far the vegetation edge will move, beyond what a statistical forecast already explains. It is trained once on all sites and serves every live AOI.

Model card

Model family rolling_hybrid_mambalstm_v1 Architecture Input projection, 3 Mamba-style blocks, 1-layer LSTM, MLP head Parameters 192,641 Task Predict the error of the statistical base forecast for one transect at one horizon Input 12 monthly steps of base residuals over 27 neighbouring transects (390 m of coast), plus 16 context features Output One correction in metres, scaled by a per-horizon gate Horizons 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months Training data 15 AOIs, Sentinel-2 history 2016 to 2026, rolling-origin splits with no look-ahead Result Lowest held-out RMSE of all methods tested at every horizon (Training & Evaluation)

docs.title: The hybrid forecast
docs.text:
TERRA Coastal DT does not ask a neural network to forecast the coastline from scratch. Instead, it combines a statistical base forecast that is refitted at every request with a learned correction from MambaLSTM:

\[ \hat{y}_j(t_0 + h) \;=\; \underbrace{\ell_j(t_0) \;+\; s_j(t_0 + h) \;+\; \phi^{\Delta}\, e_j(t_0)}_{\text{statistical base}} \;+\; g_h \; \underbrace{f_\theta\!\left(\mathbf{R}_j, \mathbf{M}_j, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{z}_{j,h}\right)}_{\text{MambaLSTM correction}} \] Symbol Meaning \(\hat{y}_j(t_0+h)\) Forecast vegetation-edge distance on transect \(j\), \(h\) months after the forecast origin \(t_0\) (the p50 line) \(\ell_j(t_0)\) Current level: the transect's fitted trend line evaluated at the origin. The trend sets where the edge is now but is not extrapolated \(s_j(t_0+h)\) Seasonal cycle at the target month (two harmonics per transect) \(\phi^{\Delta} e_j(t_0)\) Short-term memory: the last residual, decaying with the lag \(\Delta\) to the target month (AR(1), \(\phi \le 0.95\)) \(f_\theta(\cdot)\) MambaLSTM output: the predicted error of the base forecast \(\mathbf{R}_j, \mathbf{M}_j\) 12-month history of base residuals over the 27-transect patch centred on \(j\), and its observation mask \(\mathbf{a}\) Age of each history step relative to the origin \(\mathbf{z}_{j,h}\) 16 context features (calendar, horizon, position, trend, seasonality, data coverage, short-term memory) \(g_h\) Per-horizon gate in \([0, 1]\), fitted on held-out data

The p10 and p90 bounds are added around the p50 line using calibrated error quantiles for that AOI and horizon (see Uncertainty).

docs.title: Why a hybrid design
docs.text:
• The easy part is solved in closed form. Level, seasonality and short-term memory are well described by a small statistical model that is refitted on the AOI's whole record at every request. New observations change the forecast immediately, with no retraining.
  • The network learns only what is left. MambaLSTM is trained on the base forecast's own errors. If it predicted zero, the hybrid would reproduce the base exactly, so the network cannot make things worse by forgetting what the base already knows.
  • The gate limits harm. At each horizon the correction is scaled by the least-squares weight \(g_h = \mathrm{clip}\big(\langle y, p\rangle / \langle p, p\rangle,\, 0,\, 1\big)\) between the base's errors \(y\) and the network's predictions \(p\) on held-out data. Where the network has learned nothing transferable, \(g_h\) falls towards zero and the hybrid falls back to the base.
  • One model for every site. The network is global across AOIs; each AOI's own behaviour enters through its data. That gives the network 15 sites' worth of training examples and lets it learn patterns that a single short record could not reveal.

docs.title: What the correction learns
docs.text:
Analysis of the base forecast's errors shows two slow signals hidden under month-to-month noise:

  1. Persistent level offsets. When a stretch of coast has sat seaward (or landward) of its fitted level over the past year, about 40 to 60% of that offset persists 12 to 24 months later.
  2. Trend reversion. Fast-moving transects tend to slow down: the realised change reverts by roughly half the fitted trend.

Neither is visible in a single month's residual, which is why simple autoregressive terms miss them. MambaLSTM reads a year of residuals across 390 m of coast and picks up both, together with alongshore context: neighbouring transects move together over about 90 to 105 m.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    I["Monthly token x 12 steps<br/>27 residuals + 27 mask bits + age<br/>(55 values)"] --> P["Linear projection 55 to 64"]
    P --> B1["MambaLite block 1"]
    B1 --> B2["MambaLite block 2"]
    B2 --> B3["MambaLite block 3"]
    B3 --> L["LSTM, hidden 64"]
    L --> C["Context at the last observed step"]
    S["16 context features"] --> H
    C --> H["MLP head: 80 to 64, GELU, dropout, 64 to 1"]
    H --> O["Correction (m)"]
    O --> G["x gate g_h"]
Stage Layer Shape Parameters Input One token per month: patch residuals, mask, age in years 12 x 55 Projection Linear 55 to 64 3,584 Temporal mixing 3 MambaLite blocks (below) 12 x 64 150,528 Sequence memory LSTM, 1 layer 64 to 64 33,280 Read-out Hidden state at the last observed month 64 Head Concatenate 16 context features; Linear, GELU, Dropout 0.15, Linear 80 to 64 to 1 5,249 Total 192,641

docs.title: MambaLite block
docs.text:
Each block is a lightweight, Mamba-inspired temporal mixer with a residual connection:

h   = LayerNorm(x)
h   = causal depthwise Conv1d(h, kernel 4)      # each channel sees only the current and 3 previous months
a,b = split(Linear 64 -> 512 (h))               # two 256-wide halves
x   = x + Dropout( Linear 256 -> 64 ( tanh(a) * sigmoid(b) ) )

The causal convolution mixes information across neighbouring months without looking into the future. The gated MLP (\(\tanh \odot \sigma\)) lets the block decide, feature by feature, how much of that mixed signal to pass on. Three blocks give each step a receptive field of 10 months before the LSTM summarises the whole sequence. The block keeps the gating and causal convolution of Mamba but replaces its selective state-space scan with a short convolution, which suits the 12-step monthly sequences used here.

docs.title: Handling missing data
docs.text:
Cloud cover means many months have no observation for some or all transects.

  • Each token carries the observation mask, so the network knows which values are real.
  • Months with no observation anywhere in the patch are gated to zero before and after every block, so they contribute nothing.
  • The read-out takes the LSTM state at the last observed month, not at a padded position.
  • Each token carries its age, so irregular gaps between observations are visible to the network.
  • Inputs are scaled and clipped, so an occasional extraction failure of 100 m or more cannot dominate a sequence.

docs.title: Context features
docs.text:
The 16 per-sample features give the head information that is not in the residual history:

Group Features Calendar Annual and semi-annual harmonics (sin, cos) of the origin month and of the target month (8) Horizon Forecast horizon in years Position Normalised position along the AOI; distance to the AOI end (km) Transect behaviour Fitted trend per year; seasonal amplitude Data coverage Fraction of the patch history that was observed Short-term memory The base's AR term; its coefficient \(\phi\)

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
The p10 and p90 bounds use split-conformal calibration. The hybrid's own errors on a held-out calibration period give error quantiles (5, 10, 50, 90 and 95%) for each AOI and horizon. An AOI-specific quantile is used when at least 200 calibration errors are available; otherwise the pooled quantile across AOIs is used. Calibrating per AOI matters: a pooled band would be half as wide as it should be at the most dynamic site.

On test data the nominal 80% band (p10 to p90) covers 72 to 76% of outcomes, so it is slightly narrow. See Training & Evaluation.

docs.title: Serving
docs.text:
At every forecast request the service:

  1. loads the active model package (weights, gates, calibration) from the model registry;
  2. adds the newest accepted observation to the AOI's monthly series;
  3. refits the statistical base on the whole record up to that observation;
  4. builds the MambaLSTM inputs with the same code used in training, so training and serving cannot drift apart;
  5. computes base + gated correction for every transect, then the p10 and p90 bounds;
  6. reconstructs forecast lines and erosion-risk areas (where the p10 line lies landward of the current edge) on the map.

Inference is light (one forward pass per transect and horizon on CPU). Horizons beyond 24 months are served with the correction and interval of the longest trained horizon for the same calendar month, and are flagged horizon_extrapolated, because the intervals were never calibrated that far out.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The correction is a refinement: it improves the base by 2.9 to 6.5% RMSE. Most forecast skill comes from fixing the measurement frame and modelling level and seasonality correctly.
  • Uncertainty bands are slightly narrow (72 to 76% coverage for a nominal 80%).
  • The model sees only the coastline's own history. Storms, surges and wave climate are not yet inputs, so abrupt event-driven change is not anticipated.
  • The model is trained on Scottish dune coasts. Other coastal types need validation before use.

See Model Lifecycle for how model versions are packaged, registered, promoted and retrained.

docs.title: Model Lifecycle
docs.text:
This page describes how a trained MambaLSTM model becomes the model that serves forecasts, how it stays current as new observations arrive, and how a new version replaces it.

flowchart LR
    A["Train<br/>rolling-origin protocol"] --> B["Model package<br/>weights, gates,<br/>calibration, report"]
    B --> C["Publish<br/>MinIO object +<br/>registry entry"]
    C --> D["Active version<br/>serves forecasts"]
    D --> E["New observations<br/>absorbed by the base"]
    E --> D
    D -. "enough new data" .-> A
    D -. "rollback" .-> F["Previous version"]

docs.title: Model package
docs.text:
A model version is a self-contained package:

File Content best.pth Network weights, target scale, per-horizon gates and the input layout the network expects summary.json Model family (rolling_hybrid_mambalstm_v1), architecture, AOIs, horizons, gates, parameter count and test results calibration.json Conformal error quantiles per AOI and horizon, and pooled across AOIs validation.json Full rolling-origin test report for every method, per horizon and per AOI

Because the gates and calibration travel with the weights, a package always serves exactly the forecast that was evaluated.

docs.title: Registry and serving
docs.text:
• Packages are stored as objects in MinIO; each version is registered in the MongoDB model_versions collection with its checksum, provenance and the dataset version it was trained on.
  • Each AOI has one active model version. The registry decides which forecaster serves an AOI: the active version's model family selects the MambaLSTM hybrid, or the legacy statistical forecaster used by retired AOIs.
  • The serving container downloads the active package on first use, verifies it, and keeps it only as a replaceable cache.
  • Every forecast records the model version, dataset version and observation it was made from, so any forecast can be traced back to the exact model that produced it.

docs.title: Staying current without retraining
docs.text: New observations do not require a new model. At every request the statistical base is refitted on the AOI's whole record, including the newest accepted observation, and the MambaLSTM inputs are rebuilt from that refit. A new month therefore changes the level, the short-term memory term and the network's input window immediately. The network weights capture patterns shared across sites and change only when the model is retrained.

docs.title: Retraining the correction
docs.text:
The shared MambaLSTM correction is retrained offline, with the same rolling-origin protocol, when enough new history has accumulated or when new AOIs are added:

  1. Build the updated monthly datasets for the AOIs to include.
  2. Run the training script. It trains the network, fits the gates, calibrates the intervals and evaluates every method on the most recent 24 months.
  3. Compare the new test report with the active version's report.
  4. Publish the package to the registry.

Retraining through the asynchronous job endpoint is reserved for per-AOI legacy forecasters; for hybrid AOIs the endpoint explains that the shared correction is retrained offline. Superseded packages are kept, so earlier results remain reproducible.

docs.title: Promotion and rollback
docs.text:
Model administration is restricted to administrators (bearer token, normally issued through the platform gateway):

  • POST /models/<model_version_id>/promote promotes an evaluated candidate together with the dataset version it was trained on, in one atomic step.
  • POST /models/<model_version_id>/rollback reactivates the previous version and its dataset.
  • GET /aois/<aoi_id>/model-status reports the active version, any candidate, and retraining eligibility.

docs.text: Version AOIs Change October 2026 (active) 15 Retrained after refining the St Andrews West Sands geometry (spit tip measured, reference line rerouted round the west hook) October 2026 15 Five further AOIs added on the Clyde, Aberdeenshire, Moray and Dornoch coasts September 2026 10 First rolling hybrid: rolling statistical base with gated MambaLSTM correction

docs.title: Training & Evaluation
docs.text: This page describes how the MambaLSTM correction is trained and how the hybrid forecaster is evaluated against other methods. Every number comes from the deployed model's own training run (October 2026, 15 AOIs).

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Sites 15 AOIs (aoi_01 to aoi_15) in 8 independent coastal groups Series Monthly vegetation-edge distance per transect: the median of the month's screened scenes, with alongshore outliers rejected Samples One sample per (transect, forecast origin, horizon) Horizons 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months Look-back 12 monthly steps Patch 27 transects centred on the target (390 m at 15 m spacing) Transect stride Every 15th transect (225 m), about twice the 90 to 105 m alongshore correlation length, so sampled transects are close to independent

Every quantity attached to a sample, including the statistical base fit, the residuals and the context features, is computed only from data at or before the sample's forecast origin. The model never sees the future it is asked to predict.

docs.title: Rolling-origin splits
docs.text:
Splits are made by target month, counted back from the end of each AOI's record:

flowchart LR
    T["Training<br/>targets before the last 42 months<br/>45,478 samples"] --> V["Inner validation<br/>18 months<br/>24,406 samples"] --> X["Test<br/>last 24 months<br/>34,628 samples"]
  • Training samples fit the network weights.
  • Inner validation samples choose the training epoch, fit the per-horizon gates and calibrate the uncertainty intervals.
  • Test samples are used once, for the results below.

Forecasts are issued from every origin in the test period (about 290 origins per horizon), as they would have been in operation. Errors are aggregated per origin, then per AOI, then across AOIs, so every site counts equally however long its coastline.

An independent check moves the whole scheme 24 months earlier and discards everything after it. On the earlier 10-AOI configuration the ranking of methods held in that window as well.

docs.title: Optimisation
docs.text:
Setting Value Target The base forecast's error, scaled by its standard deviation (11.7 m) Loss Huber loss (\(\delta = 1\)) on the scaled target Optimiser AdamW, learning rate \(10^{-3}\), weight decay \(10^{-3}\) Batch size 512 Gradient clipping Norm 1.0 Epochs Up to 20, early stopping with patience 5 on inner-validation RMSE Selected epoch 5 (inner RMSE 11.13 m against 11.74 m for predicting zero, a 5.2% gain)

After training, the per-horizon gates are fitted on the inner split:

Horizon 1 month 3 months 6 months 12 months 24 months Gate \(g_h\) 0.62 0.96 0.88 1.00 1.00

The correction is used at nearly full weight from 3 months on. At 1 month the base's short-term memory term already explains much of the error, so the correction is scaled down.

docs.title: Methods compared
docs.text:
All methods are trained and scored under the same rolling-origin protocol on the same samples.

Method Description Persistence No change: the last observation is the forecast Trend only Each transect's straight-line trend, extrapolated Naive LSTM A univariate LSTM (37,825 parameters): one transect's own 12-month history and the horizon, with no neighbours, calendar or statistical base Base The statistical base alone: level + seasonal cycle + AR(1) memory, refitted at every origin Hybrid (MambaLSTM) Base + gated MambaLSTM correction: the deployed model

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Test RMSE in metres (lower is better):

Horizon Persistence Trend only Naive LSTM Base Hybrid (MambaLSTM) 1 month 10.10 11.54 10.25 9.47 9.15 3 months 14.06 12.17 11.44 11.00 10.54 6 months 16.63 12.70 12.34 11.46 11.12 12 months 12.89 12.89 11.23 11.61 10.86 24 months 14.07 15.07 12.68 12.87 12.11

Reduction in RMSE achieved by the hybrid:

Horizon vs persistence vs trend only vs naive LSTM vs base 1 month 9.3% 20.7% 10.7% 3.4% 3 months 25.1% 13.4% 7.9% 4.2% 6 months 33.2% 12.4% 9.9% 2.9% 12 months 15.7% 15.8% 3.3% 6.5% 24 months 13.9% 19.6% 4.5% 5.9%

Number of AOIs (out of 15) where the hybrid has lower test RMSE:

Horizon vs base vs naive LSTM 1 month 13 9 3 months 11 12 6 months 9 14 12 months 12 8 24 months 12 9

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
• The hybrid is the most accurate method at every horizon. The gain over the statistical base is largest at 12 and 24 months (6.5% and 5.9%), where the slow level offsets and trend reversion that MambaLSTM learns matter most.
  • Structure beats a bigger black box. The naive LSTM has the same sequence length but sees only one transect and no statistical base. The hybrid beats it by 8 to 11% at 1 to 6 months and by 3 to 5% at 12 to 24 months.
  • Extrapolating trends hurts. Trend-only is worse than persistence at 1 and 24 months. Trends fitted on the two halves of a record correlate at only -0.49 to +0.33, which is why the base sets the current level from the trend but does not extrapolate it.
  • Persistence is strong at 12 months because a same-month observation one year earlier already carries the seasonal state. The hybrid still improves on it by 15.7%.

docs.title: Interval coverage
docs.text:
Share of test outcomes inside the p10 to p90 band (nominal 80%):

Horizon 1 month 3 months 6 months 12 months 24 months Coverage 76% 75% 74% 74% 72%

The bands are slightly narrow because the inner split that calibrates them is also used to choose the epoch and the gates. A separate calibration period would correct this at the cost of training data.

docs.title: Lessons from model development
docs.text:
Several design decisions were settled by experiments under this protocol:

  • Earlier static baselines were optimistic. A baseline fitted once on the whole record leaked future information into its own evaluation. The rolling, refit-at-every-origin base removed that look-ahead and is what all results above use.
  • Predicting the base's error works better than predicting the edge. Residual models trained against a static baseline, including a 16,000-parameter convolutional model and an earlier MambaLSTM, early-stopped within 3 epochs at about the skill of predicting zero. Training against the rolling base's own error, with the gate, is what made the correction pay off.
  • Not extrapolating the trend cut 24-month RMSE by 9 to 16% against a full-trend baseline in two independent test windows.

docs.title: Reproducing
docs.text: The training script scripts/train_hybrid_forecast.py in the source repository runs the whole protocol and writes a model package (weights, gates, calibration, validation report). --shift-months 24 runs the independent earlier window.

docs.title: Intelligent Coastal Digital Twin Orchestration
docs.text: This component makes the processing capabilities behave as one digital twin: it keeps each AOI's coastal state current, coordinates observation, assimilation, forecasting and validation, and exposes the results to users and to the TERRA platform.

docs.title: The digital twin loop
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    O["Observe<br/>new scene assets"] --> A["Assimilate<br/>extract, accept or reject"]
    A --> S["State<br/>observations in MongoDB,<br/>artifacts in MinIO"]
    S --> F["Forecast<br/>MambaLSTM hybrid"]
    F --> V["Validate and review<br/>retrospective cases,<br/>observation review"]
    V --> M["Model lifecycle<br/>promote or roll back"]
    M --> F
    S --> O
  1. Observe. New scenes arrive from the TERRA ingestion service as committed scene assets, or on demand from the web interface.
  2. Assimilate. POST /jobs/assimilate processes the new assets for an AOI, oldest first. Each scene is checked against acquisitions already observed, extracted with the AOI's pinned parameters, and either committed as an observation or recorded as rejected with its reasons.
  3. Update state. Accepted observations and their per-transect measurements are written to MongoDB; rasters, previews and GeoJSON are stored in MinIO. The container itself holds no durable state.
  4. Forecast. The next forecast refits the statistical base on the updated record and applies the MambaLSTM correction (see MambaLSTM Forecasting Model).
  5. Validate and review. Retrospective validation tests forecasts against later observations; operators can review individual observations.
  6. Model lifecycle. New model versions are published, promoted or rolled back through the model registry (see Model Lifecycle).

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Long-running work runs as persistent asynchronous jobs:

  • each job has an identifier, ordered phase events and a final result, stored in MongoDB;
  • clients poll GET /jobs/<job_id>;
  • submissions accept an idempotency key, so a retried request does not create duplicate work;
  • jobs left running by a stopped container are detected as stale and marked failed.
Job Purpose POST /jobs/assimilate Assimilate committed scene assets into an AOI's state POST /jobs/extract Extract the vegetation edge from given scenes of an AOI POST /jobs/predict Run a forecast POST /jobs/retrain Train candidate models for per-AOI legacy forecasters (the shared MambaLSTM is retrained offline)

docs.title: Platform orchestration
docs.text: In the TERRA platform, Apache Airflow is the control plane. A daily chain calls the TERRA ingestion service with the UC3 profile, skips quietly when no new scene exists, submits the committed scene assets to POST /jobs/assimilate, and reports accepted, rejected and duplicate observations. Forecasting remains a user or service action, and model promotion remains an explicit administrator decision. The service's in-process scheduler is disabled in platform deployments and kept only for local development.

docs.title: User interfaces
docs.text:
• Forecast (/): select an AOI, extract the latest observation, load history, forecast, and compare historical coastlines.
  • Validation (/validation): run retrospective cases and compare the hybrid with other methods.
  • Baseline geometry (/baseline-workflow): inspect and prepare reference lines and transects.

See Forecast Workflow and Retrospective Validation.

docs.title: AI-enabled Satellite Image Processing
docs.text:
This component turns an AOI request into screened, analysis-ready Sentinel-2 imagery for vegetation-edge extraction. It is the first runtime step of the product chain.

AOI -> catalogue search -> AOI-level cloud screening -> 5-band download -> preflight checks -> scene asset

docs.title: Component role
docs.text:
• search the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE) catalogue for Sentinel-2 L2A scenes over an AOI;
  • screen candidate scenes for cloud over the AOI itself, not just over the whole satellite tile;
  • download the bands the vegetation classifier needs, clipped to the AOI;
  • check every raster structurally and for coastal usability before it is used;
  • record accepted and rejected scenes, with reasons, so every observation is traceable.

docs.title: Data source
docs.text: Mission Sentinel-2, Level-2A surface reflectance Provider Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel Hub catalogue and processing APIs) Bands B02 (blue), B03 (green), B04 (red), B08 (near infrared), B11 (short-wave infrared), delivered as one 5-band reflectance raster Screening layer Scene Classification Layer (SCL)

docs.title: AOI-level cloud screening
docs.text: A Sentinel-2 tile covers about 110 x 110 km, while an AOI covers around 18 km² of coast, about 0.15% of the tile. The tile's cloud figure is therefore a weak guide: the same acquisition has been reported as 54% cloudy on one tile and 24% on its neighbour over identical AOI pixels. The component therefore uses the tile's cloud percentage only as a loose pre-filter, then requests a low-resolution (60 m) probe of the SCL layer over the AOI and computes the share of unusable pixels inside it: medium and high cloud, cloud shadow, thin cirrus, no data, saturated pixels, and snow or ice. Only scenes under the AOI-level limit are downloaded at full resolution, so rejected scenes cost one small request.

docs.title: Three acquisition paths
docs.text:
Historical archiveLatest observation (on demand)Scheduled ingestion (TERRA platform)

Monthly pulls build each AOI's history from 2016 onwards: tile pre-filter at 80% cloud, AOI-level limit of 20%, and up to three scenes per month. Failures raise errors instead of falling back to synthetic data.

When a user asks for the latest state, the service searches a recent window (120 days by default), probes the newest candidates with AOI-level screening, and accepts the newest scene that passes screening and extraction. A deployment can tighten the AOI cloud limit (10% in operation). Repeated requests within a cache window reuse the accepted observation without another catalogue call.

In the platform deployment, the TERRA ingestion service runs the UC3 acquisition profile coastal-uc3-sentinel2 on a schedule, commits accepted scenes to shared storage, and asks the digital twin to assimilate them. See Data Ingestion.

docs.title: Preflight checks
docs.text:
Before a raster is used, it must pass:

  • structural checks: expected band count, data type, georeferencing and AOI coverage;
  • coastal checks: enough valid pixels, and enough vegetation (NDVI) contrast for an edge to be measurable;
  • duplicate checks: a scene acquired at the same time as one already observed is not processed twice (matched by acquisition time within 3 minutes, because one satellite pass can appear under two tile identifiers).

Rejected scenes are recorded with their reasons, so a missing month can be explained.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• accepted scene metadata and quality diagnostics;
  • 5-band AOI rasters stored as immutable objects;
  • preview images for the map;
  • scene-evaluation records for accepted and rejected candidates.

docs.title: Coastal Change Time-Series Analysis and Forecasting
docs.text:
This component turns the vegetation-edge record of each AOI into monthly per-transect time series, forecasts the edge 1 to 24 months ahead with the MambaLSTM hybrid forecaster, and supports retrospective validation of those forecasts.

VE observations -> monthly series per transect -> statistical base + MambaLSTM correction -> p10 / p50 / p90 -> maps, erosion risk, validation

docs.title: Monthly time series
docs.text:
Scenes arrive irregularly because of cloud. For forecasting, each AOI's record is turned into a regular monthly series:

  • monthly composite: the median of the month's accepted scenes for every transect;
  • alongshore outlier rejection: a value that disagrees strongly with its alongshore neighbours in the same month is removed, because real change is coherent over about 100 m of coast while extraction errors are not;
  • patch layout: each transect is stored with its neighbourhood of 27 transects (390 m), the input unit of the MambaLSTM model;
  • versioned datasets: each dataset version records its extraction parameters and time span, and the model that serves an AOI is pinned to a dataset version.

docs.title: Forecasting
docs.text:
Forecasts are produced by the hybrid forecaster described in MambaLSTM Forecasting Model:

\[ \text{p50} \;=\; \underbrace{\text{level} + \text{season} + \text{short-term memory}}_{\text{refitted at every request}} \;+\; g_h \cdot \text{MambaLSTM correction} \]
  • The statistical base is refitted on the AOI's whole record up to the newest observation at every request, so the forecast always starts from the current state.
  • The MambaLSTM correction, trained on all 15 AOIs, adds what the base misses: persistent level offsets, trend reversion and alongshore context.
  • p10 and p90 come from conformal error quantiles calibrated per AOI and horizon.
Horizon Test RMSE (hybrid) Improvement over the base Improvement over persistence 1 month 9.15 m 3.4% 9.3% 3 months 10.54 m 4.2% 25.1% 6 months 11.12 m 2.9% 33.2% 12 months 10.86 m 6.5% 15.7% 24 months 12.11 m 5.9% 13.9%

Full results and the comparison with a plain LSTM are in Training & Evaluation.

docs.title: Forecast products
docs.text:
Product Description Forecast lines p50 (median), p10 and p90 vegetation-edge lines reconstructed on the map from transect distances Uncertainty band The area between p10 and p90 Erosion-risk areas Polygons where the conservative p10 forecast lies landward of the current vegetation edge Forecast table Per-transect p10 / p50 / p90 distances, stored as queryable measurements Historical coastlines The vegetation edge in the same calendar month of each of the last N years, with the median net change between the first and last year

Horizons beyond 24 months are returned with a horizon_extrapolated flag, because the intervals are only calibrated up to 24 months.

docs.title: Historical coastlines
docs.text: Comparing the same month every year removes the seasonal cycle (5 to 33% of the temporal variance at these sites), so the differences between lines show year-to-year change and measurement noise. If a year lacks that month because of cloud, the adjacent month is used and labelled. Lines are smoothed over about 100 m, the measured alongshore correlation length, so per-transect noise is removed while real coastal shape is kept.
